Container.Name: minstrel-launchpad
Container.Overview:
Reach your own music from outside the house. minstrel-launchpad sits on your network beside your UPnP/DLNA media server (MinimServer, Gerbera, Plex's DLNA, a NAS's own server) and lets the Minstrel app browse and play from it while you are away, over TLS pinned to this launchpad's own certificate. Only devices you have paired, by scanning a QR code on your own network, can connect; there is no account and no third party in the path. Where a port cannot be opened — carrier-grade NAT, for instance — it can fall back to a relay you run yourself.
Needs host networking: media servers are found with SSDP multicast, which a Docker bridge network does not carry.
After starting it, open the container log for a one-time link that sets the console password.
Container.Description:
Reach your own music from outside the house.
minstrel-launchpad sits beside your UPnP/DLNA media server and lets the Minstrel app browse and play from it while you are away. Traffic is TLS pinned to this launchpad's own certificate, and only devices paired by scanning a QR code on your own network can connect. No account, no cloud, nothing sent anywhere you did not choose.
• Works with any UPnP/DLNA media server on the same network • ffmpeg is included, so it can send a smaller copy over mobile data • Optional self-hosted relay for homes behind carrier-grade NAT • Web console for pairing, naming devices and revoking them
Open the container log after first start for the console setup link.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Pairings, the launchpad's TLS key and its settings. Keep it: recreating the container with an empty one unpairs every device.
